example-letter.typ

A conformance sample for the Typst implementation — letter() template, justified, page-foot footnote. Rendered below from typeset.typ; the checker compiles it fresh on every commit.

The rendered pages are not available here — the source is below. To build them in a checkout, run node tools/build-previews.mjs with Typst on PATH.

32 lines · 1.6 KB

1// A conformance check for the letter template: letter() sets the page, the
2// letterhead and the sign-off from its parameters, and the body is the
3// letter. Justified at 12pt, no running head, no folio, and a real footnote
4// at the foot of the page.
5#import "typeset.typ": *
6
7#show: letter.with(
8 // A crest is optional. This placeholder is drawn in one ink, so svg-recolor
9 // sets it in the accent; read() resolves the path against this file.
10 crest: svg-recolor(read("crest-placeholder.svg"), width: 100%),
11 sender: ("Adilson Carvalho", "10 Wentworth Avenue", "Surry Hills NSW 2010", "Australia"),
12 addressee: ("The Registrar", "Institute of Typographic Studies", "88 Rundle Street", "Adelaide SA 5000"),
13 date: "27 August 2026",
14 saint: "St Monica, mother of St Augustine Bishop",
15 salutation: "Registrar",
16 signature: "Adilson Carvalho",
17 enclosures: [typeset.css; two specimen pages],
18 postscript: [The tables were excellent — tabular figures throughout.],
19)
20
21I am writing about the setting of the Institute's annual report, which arrived
22this morning and which I read with rather more attention to its margins than to
23its contents.
24
25The text column runs to something near a hundred and ten
26characters.#footnote[Measured on page four, between the outer margins: 168mm at
27a 10pt body, which is about 112 characters.] By the second page I had lost my
28place twice, and by the fourth I had stopped reading and started measuring.
29
30This is a cheap problem to fix. Narrowing the column to sixty-six characters
31costs one afternoon and no money, and the space it frees on the right can carry
32the marginal notes that are currently crowded into footnotes.
